subject: EdgeCore: sudden request queue growth / p99 spikes — action plan
messages:
From: Ari Kaplan <ari@edgecore.ai>

Cc: platform@edgecore.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: High p99s + queued requests this morning (production)

Hi Priyom —

We're seeing a sustained increase in our P99 generation latency starting ~09:45 PT and it looks correlated with a sudden build-up of queued requests in the Redwood tenant pool for EdgeCore. Quick facts from our dashboard:
- P95 ~ 650ms (normal), P99 jumped to ~18s (normally ~800ms)
- Error rate (5xx) rose from 0.2% -> 1.8% in the window
- Throughput dropped ~25% while client-side retries increased

We captured a few trace IDs (attached) and a CSV excerpt of request timing around the incident. The transact workflow is latency-sensitive — the customer experience impact is visible. Can you please:
1) confirm you see the same build-up on your side
2) provide short-term mitigations (routing, fallback, concurrency changes) we can apply immediately
3) a follow-up on root cause and timeline for fix

We're on standby for a call.

Thanks,
Ari Kaplan
Head of Platform — EdgeCore Robotics

- Temporarily routed EdgeCore traffic to a warm reserve pool to relieve queuing (in progress).

- Marissa (Solutions) and Monica (SRE) are engaged to coordinate a mitigation runbook.

I'll schedule a 30-min sync in ~30 minutes to walk through actions and timeline. Laura is looped for visibility.

Folks — quick initial hypotheses from the ops side (based on telemetry we pulled):
- Autoscaler did not spin additional pods because per-pod concurrency cap hit its configured max; scheduler thought pods were healthy but saturated.
- We see an unusual mix of many short-streaming requests with long context lengths from EdgeCore's workload — this increases KV cache pressure and reduces effective throughput.
- There are a handful of backend GPUs showing increased queue depth consistent with backpressure (we're attaching a metrics snapshot).

Suggested immediate mitigations:
1) Bump per-pod concurrency cap for the EdgeCore tenant pool from 16 -> 32 for the next 2 hours.
2) Route ~25% of their traffic to a warm reserve pool (already in motion).
3) If routing + cap bump insufficient, enable fallback to a light-weight model variant for non-critical endpoints to lower token time.

Operational asks for engineering (Laura):
- Approve a temporary concurrency cap change and confirm there are no infra-side constraints.
- If approved, ops can execute the bump and monitor queue depth.

I can own the execution and monitoring. Attaching autoscale-metrics-20280721.png and an excerpt.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99s + queued requests this morning (production)

Update after quick triage:
- Root cause (short): per-pod concurrency limit + prefix/KV cache churn. Autoscaler thresholds were met (CPU/req-per-sec) but scale-up did not happen because all current pods were reporting healthy and concurrency was saturated at the pod level.
- Evidence: request-trace-20280721.json shows a pattern where many requests open streaming connections, hold KV cache state, then release — resulting in cache thrash and serialization delays for remote KV reads.

Actions executed (16:05 PT):
- Increased concurrency cap for the tenant pool to 32 (temporary, 2-hour window).
- Routed 30% of EdgeCore traffic to warm-reserve pool.
- Enabled aggressive prefix cache retention for the pool to reduce KV cache misses.

Immediate effect: P99 reduced from ~18s -> ~2.6s in the first 10 minutes; error rate trending down. We'll continue to monitor and revert any temporary changes after the window.

Next steps (post-stabilize):
- Engineering to investigate autoscaler interaction with pod-level concurrency (Laura).
- Product/solutions to review model/endpoint configuration for EdgeCore to reduce KV churn (Marissa).
- We will produce a formal RCA and a proposed config change package (concurrency + caching + routing) so this doesn't recur.

Trace ID for one representative request: trace-edgecore-7f2b1a5 (attached).

—Monica
SRE, Redwood Inference

Ari — quick update and apology on behalf of the team.

What we did (summary):
- Executed temporary mitigations (concurrency cap bump, partial routing to warm pool, adjusted prefix cache) between 16:05–16:20 PT on Jul 21.
- Observed P99 drop from ~18s -> ~2.6s and error rate decline; we've kept mitigations active while we complete the RCA.

Why it happened (short):
- The tenant pool encountered a pattern of streaming, high-context requests that increased KV cache churn and saturated per-pod concurrency limits. The autoscaler did not scale fast enough because metrics indicated healthy pods but with saturated concurrency.

Next steps (we commit to):
1) Laura / Eng to deliver an RCA by end of day Monday (Jul 23) that includes: autoscaler behavior, suggested permanent concurrency configuration, and any runtime changes to handle streaming-heavy traffic.
2) Marissa will work with you to review endpoint configuration and test fallbacks to a lighter model variant for non-core flows.
3) We'll offer a service credit for the impact window and a technical postmortem call with our Eng/SRE leads — propose Tue 09:00 PT (please confirm).

We're sorry for the disruption. I'm available for a call now or at the times you suggest.

Thanks for flagging this early — we'll be in close touch.

—Priyom
